book.title: A Christmas Carol · Stave 4 — The Last of the Spirits
book.author: Charles Dickens, A Christmas Carol (1843)

iconic_quotes_kept: shadows of the things that Will be, or... May be
I will honour Christmas in my heart
I am not the man I was

cast.name: Scrooge
cast.role: old miser, now terrified and repenting
cast.canonical: a thin bent elderly man, completely bald on top with wispy grey side-hair, a long smooth clean-shaven face and a sharp pointed nose, in a plain striped knee-length nightshirt, barefoot, bare-headed
cast.anchor: thin bent bald clean-shaven old man, sharp nose, striped nightshirt, barefoot
cast.distinct_from: the old bald Scrooge — not a ghost, not a giant

cast.name: Ghost of Christmas Yet to Come
cast.canonical: a tall silent phantom draped from head to foot in a deep black hooded shroud, its whole face and body hidden in blackness, only one pale outstretched hand visible, pointing; it never speaks
cast.anchor: tall black hooded faceless phantom, whole figure in a black shroud, only one pale pointing hand
cast.distinct_from: faceless and silent in a solid black shroud — no face, no torch, no light, unlike every other spirit

cast.name: Bob Cratchit
cast.canonical: a thin gentle clerk with dark hair and a mild kind face, wound in a long white knitted comforter scarf, in a threadbare coat
cast.anchor: thin dark-haired clerk, long white comforter scarf
cast.distinct_from: a grown thin clerk — not bald, not a phantom

panels.scene: a tall silent phantom draped head to foot in a deep black hooded shroud, its face hidden in darkness, only one pale hand reaching out to point, looming in a dark street

teen.narration: THE LAST SPIRIT CAME — SILENT, HOODED, AND FACELESS.

bubbles.text: It said nothing, and only pointed. Scrooge feared this one most of all.

panels.scene: the bald pointed-nosed old man in a striped nightshirt, barefoot, trembling as he follows the tall black hooded phantom whose pale hand points the way through a dark city street

teen.narration: IT LED SCROOGE ON, ITS POINTING HAND NEVER STILL.

bubbles.speaker: SCROOGE
bubbles.text: Ghost of the Future — I fear you more than any spirit I have seen.

panels.scene: a group of well-fed businessmen in top hats standing on a city street, chatting and chuckling carelessly, unbothered
panels.composition: scene — careless talk of a death

teen.narration: SOME BUSINESSMEN SPOKE OF A DEATH — CARELESSLY.

bubbles.text: 'When did he die?' 'Last night, I believe.' 'What has he done with all his money?'

panels.scene: two of the top-hatted businessmen laughing together and turning away, one waving a careless hand

teen.narration: THEY LAUGHED. NO ONE SEEMED SORRY THE MAN WAS DEAD.

bubbles.text: 'It will be a cheap funeral — I'll only go if lunch is provided!'

panels.scene: a filthy dim rag-and-bone shop where a couple of ragged thieves and a charwoman haggle over a bundle of a dead man's belongings with a greasy old dealer
panels.composition: scene — selling the dead man's things

teen.narration: IN A FILTHY SHOP, THIEVES SOLD OFF A DEAD MAN'S THINGS.

bubbles.text: His bed-curtains, his blankets, even the shirt off his back — all stolen and sold.

panels.scene: a bare cold gloomy room where a dead body lies alone under a thin plain sheet on a stripped and plundered bed, no mourners, no light but a chink of pale moon

teen.narration: THE DEAD MAN LAY ALONE — ROBBED, UNWATCHED, UNWEPT.

bubbles.text: Not one kind soul sat beside him. Scrooge dared not lift the sheet to see the face.

panels.scene: the bald nightshirt old man shrinking back in a doorway as the tall black hooded faceless phantom stands over a sheeted body, its pale hand pointing at it
panels.composition: close — the phantom points at the corpse

bubbles.speaker: SCROOGE
bubbles.text: Spirit, this is a fearful place. Show me some tenderness at a death, or that dark room will haunt me forever.

panels.scene: a poor young husband and wife in a modest room, a look of guilty relief passing over their tired faces

teen.narration: ONE POOR COUPLE FELT ONLY RELIEF — THEY HAD OWED THE DEAD MAN MONEY.

bubbles.text: 'We are saved,' she whispered. 'God forgive us — but thank Heaven.'

panels.scene: the poor Cratchit family sitting very still and quiet, the mother in dark clothes with her sewing fallen in her lap; by the fire an empty little stool and a small child's crutch, carefully kept
panels.composition: scene — grief in the Cratchit home

teen.narration: AT THE CRATCHIT HOME, ALL WAS QUIET AND STILL.

bubbles.text: An empty stool. A little crutch, lovingly kept. Tiny Tim was gone.

panels.scene: the thin dark-haired clerk in his long white comforter scarf broken with grief, one hand pressed over his face, weeping alone in the quiet room

teen.narration: BOB CRATCHIT COULD NOT HIDE HIS BROKEN HEART.

bubbles.speaker: BOB
bubbles.text: My little, little child! My little child!

panels.scene: the dark-haired clerk in his white comforter, calmer now, gently gathering his family close, a sad tender smile through his tears

teen.narration: BUT HE PROMISED THEY WOULD NEVER FORGET TIM'S GENTLE HEART.

bubbles.speaker: BOB
bubbles.text: However far apart we drift, we shall none of us forget poor Tiny Tim.

panels.scene: the bald nightshirt old man trembling, turning to the tall black hooded faceless phantom, dread and a desperate need to understand on his face
panels.composition: close — who was the dead man?

teen.narration: SCROOGE COULD BEAR IT NO LONGER.

bubbles.speaker: SCROOGE
bubbles.text: Spirit — tell me who that lonely dead man was!

panels.scene: the tall black hooded faceless phantom standing among neglected, weed-choked graves in a bleak churchyard, its pale hand pointing straight down at one particular gravestone
panels.composition: close — the phantom points to a grave

teen.narration: THE PHANTOM LED HIM TO A NEGLECTED GRAVE — AND POINTED DOWN.

bubbles.text: Before he looked, Scrooge already dreaded whose name he would find.

panels.scene: the bald nightshirt old man on his knees in horror before a plain weathered gravestone with a blank uncarved face, clutching at its cold edge
panels.composition: close — his own name on the stone

teen.narration: SCROOGE CREPT TOWARD THE STONE — AND READ HIS OWN NAME.

bubbles.text: The neglected grave bore one name: EBENEZER SCROOGE. The lonely dead man was himself.

panels.scene: the bald nightshirt old man clinging to the phantom's black robe, weeping, his face lifted in desperate pleading

bubbles.speaker: SCROOGE
bubbles.text: Am I that man who lay upon the bed? No, Spirit! Oh no, no!

panels.scene: the bald nightshirt old man kneeling and reaching up imploringly to the silent black hooded phantom, hope and terror fighting on his face
panels.composition: close — will be, or may be?

bubbles.speaker: SCROOGE
bubbles.text: Are these the shadows of things that WILL be — or only the things that MAY be?

panels.scene: the bald nightshirt old man seizing the phantom's pale hand in both of his, his whole face streaming with tears and desperate resolve

teen.narration: HE SEIZED THE PHANTOM'S HAND, WEEPING.

bubbles.speaker: SCROOGE
bubbles.text: I will honour Christmas in my heart, and keep it all the year! I am not the man I was!

panels.scene: the tall black hooded phantom shrinking and dwindling down until it becomes a wooden bedpost, which the bald old man in his nightshirt is clutching in his own bedroom as pale dawn light fills the window
panels.composition: close — the phantom becomes a bedpost

teen.narration: THE SPIRIT SHRANK, COLLAPSED — AND DWINDLED INTO A BEDPOST.

bubbles.text: It was his own bed. His own room. And he was ALIVE — with time to set everything right!
